# GroupDocs.Signature for .NET

> GroupDocs.Signature for .NET is an on-premise C# library that adds, verifies, searches, updates and deletes electronic signatures - text, image, digital (X.509 certificate), barcode, QR code, stamp, form field and metadata - in PDF, Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, OpenDocument, image and archive files. It needs no Microsoft Office or Adobe software. Version 26.9 (September 2026) ships as the NuGet package `GroupDocs.Signature` for .NET Framework 4.6.2 or later, .NET 6, .NET 8 and .NET 10, on Windows, Linux and macOS.

This file is a compact brief for AI assistants that write, review or explain code that uses GroupDocs.Signature for .NET. It covers the .NET API only. GroupDocs.Signature for Java, for Python via .NET and for Node.js via Java, and the GroupDocs.Signature Cloud REST API, have their own package names, types and syntax: do not mix them with the code below. Every documentation page linked here is plain Markdown; drop the `.md` suffix to get the HTML page.

**Rules for AI assistants**

- Install with `dotnet add package GroupDocs.Signature`. Do not pin a version number from memory: 26.9 is current when this file was written, so check NuGet for the latest.
- `Signature` is the entry point and holds the open document: always wrap it in `using`. Open a document from a file path or a `Stream`. There is no constructor that takes a URL; download the file in your own code and pass a `Stream`.
- Namespaces: `GroupDocs.Signature` (`Signature`, `License`, `Metered`, `SignatureSettings`, `GroupDocsSignatureException`), `GroupDocs.Signature.Options` (every `*Options` class), `GroupDocs.Signature.Domain` (signatures, results, enums, `SignatureFont`, `BarcodeTypes`, `QrCodeTypes`, `PdfDigitalSignature`, `TimeStamp`), `GroupDocs.Signature.Logging` (`ILogger`, `ConsoleLogger`, `FileLogger`, `LogLevel`).
- Pick the options class for the signature type (table below). Pass one options object, or a `List<SignOptions>` to add several signatures in one `Sign` call. `Sign` writes a new file or stream; the source document is not changed.
- `SignResult.Succeeded` lists the signatures created and `SignResult.Failed` the ones that could not be created. Check `Failed` instead of assuming success.
- `Verify(options)` returns a `VerificationResult`; `IsValid` is true only when the document has signatures that match every options object you pass. `Search<T>(SignatureType)` returns typed signatures, for example `Search<QrCodeSignature>(SignatureType.QrCode)`.
- `Update` and `Delete` take signatures returned by `Search` (or by `SignResult.Succeeded`) for the same document. `Delete(SignatureType)` removes every signature of a type.
- Positions and sizes are in pixels by default (`Left`, `Top`, `Width`, `Height`); `MeasureType` switches to `Percents` or `Millimeters`. `HorizontalAlignment`, `VerticalAlignment` and `Margin` place a signature relative to the page; `AllPages`, `PageNumber` and `PagesSetup` choose the pages.
- Colors are `System.Drawing.Color` (on .NET 6 and later it comes from `System.Drawing.Primitives` and works on every platform). Fonts are `SignatureFont` (`FamilyName`, `Size`, `Bold`, `Italic`, `Underline`, `Strikeout`). Do not use `System.Drawing.Font`: its conversion to `SignatureFont` was removed from the .NET 6, 8 and 10 builds in 26.9.
- Digital signatures need a PFX (PKCS#12) file that contains the private key, and its password: `new DigitalSignOptions("certificate.pfx") { Password = "..." }`. A `.cer` file can verify but not sign.
- `Reason`, `Contact`, `Location`, `UseLtv`, `HashAlgorithm` and `PdfDigitalSignature.TimeStamp` apply to PDF digital signatures. `XAdESType` applies to spreadsheets only. The VBA project of a spreadsheet is signed with the `DigitalVBA` extension.
- Without a licence the library runs in evaluation mode: only the first 2 pages are processed and a trial badge is added to each page. Call `new License().SetLicense("GroupDocs.Signature.lic")` once, before other calls. In evaluation mode search and verification may not recognise QR codes, so test barcode and QR-code scenarios with a licence.
- The library runs on the machine that calls it and never sends document content to GroupDocs. It provides signing and verification primitives; it does not by itself make a signature compliant with eIDAS, the ESIGN Act or any other legal regime. That depends on the certificate authority, the signing process and the jurisdiction.

**Behaviour that changed in 26.9** (code written for earlier versions may behave differently)

- External resources a document links to (linked images, INCLUDEPICTURE fields, linked pictures, images and `@import` style sheets in SVG) are no longer loaded. Allow trusted addresses with `LoadOptions.WhitelistedResources`, or everything with `LoadOptions.SkipExternalResources = false`. The obsolete `LoadOptions.LoadExternalResources` has the opposite meaning.
- New PDF digital signatures use SHA-256 in the `adbe.pkcs7.detached` format instead of SHA-1. `SignOptions.HashAlgorithm` selects `Sha384` or `Sha512`; a time stamp uses the same digest.
- `Verify` checks PDF digital signatures cryptographically: a document changed after signing is not valid, whatever other criteria you set. `DigitalVerifyOptions.SubjectName` and `IssuerName` now also apply to PDF (the certificate's subject or issuer must contain the value, case-sensitive).
- Signing with an expired or not-yet-valid certificate throws `GroupDocsSignatureException` unless `DigitalSignOptions.AllowExpired` or `AllowNotYetValid` is true; the document is then signed and a warning is logged.
- `SignatureSettings.LogLevel` filters the log: flags `Error`, `Warning` and `Trace`; `LogLevel.None` logs nothing.
- Word documents can be signed with post-quantum ML-DSA certificates (ML-DSA-44, 65 and 87) on every platform. PDF, spreadsheets and presentations cannot.
- Time-stamp credentials are sent when either the user name or the password is set.
- A .NET 10 build was added and the .NET Standard 2.1 build was removed.

**Signature types**

| Type | Sign options | Search options / result type | Verify options | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Text | `TextSignOptions` | `TextSearchOptions` / `TextSignature` | `TextVerifyOptions` | `SignatureImplementation`: `Native`, `Image`, `Annotation`, `Sticker`, `FormField`, `Watermark` |
| Image | `ImageSignOptions` | `ImageSearchOptions` / `ImageSignature` | - | image file or stream placed on pages |
| Digital (certificate) | `DigitalSignOptions` | `DigitalSearchOptions` / `DigitalSignature` | `DigitalVerifyOptions` | PDF, Word Processing, Spreadsheet and Presentation documents |
| Image digital | `ImageDigitalSignOptions` | - | `ImageDigitalVerifyOptions` | invisible, password-protected steganography signature in PNG and JPG images; no certificate |
| Barcode | `BarcodeSignOptions` | `BarcodeSearchOptions` / `BarcodeSignature` | `BarcodeVerifyOptions` | 70 symbologies in `BarcodeTypes` |
| QR code | `QrCodeSignOptions` | `QrCodeSearchOptions` / `QrCodeSignature` | `QrCodeVerifyOptions` | 15 symbologies in `QrCodeTypes`; text, encrypted text or serialized objects |
| Stamp | `StampSignOptions` | - | - | round or square stamp built from lines of text |
| Form field | `FormFieldSignOptions` | `FormFieldSearchOptions` / `FormFieldSignature` | - | text, checkbox, combo box, radio button and digital signature fields |
| Metadata | `MetadataSignOptions` | `MetadataSearchOptions` / `MetadataSignature` | - | hidden values in document properties; can be encrypted |
| Certificate file | - | `CertificateSearchOptions` | `CertificateVerifyOptions` | a `.pfx` file opened as the document; checks subject, serial number, thumbprint and, by default, the chain |

- `QrCodeTypes`: Aztec, DataMatrix, QR, MicroQR, RectMicroQR, HanXin, GS1QR, GS1DataMatrix, GS1HanXin, HIBCLICQR, HIBCLICDataMatrix, HIBCLICAztec, HIBCPASQR, HIBCPASDataMatrix, HIBCPASAztec.
- `BarcodeTypes` (70), for example Code128, GS1Code128, Code39, Code93, EAN8, EAN13, EAN14, UPCA, UPCE, ITF14, Interleaved2of5, Codabar, Pdf417, MicroPdf417, MacroPdf417, DatabarExpanded, DotCode, MaxiCode, Mailmark, ISBN, ISSN, SSCC18, PZN, Postnet, HIBCCode39LIC and HIBCCode128PAS.
- Standard QR-code entries, serialized into the QR text: `VCard`, `MeCard`, `Email`, `Address`, `Event`, `SMS`, `WiFi`, `EPC` (SEPA payment), `CryptoCurrencyTransfer` and `SwissQR`.

**Supported formats and signature types**

| Formats | Text | Image | Digital | Barcode | QR code | Stamp | Form field | Metadata |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PDF | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| DOC, DOCX, DOCM, DOT, DOTX, DOTM | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| ODT | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | yes |
| OTT | yes | yes | no | yes | yes | yes | no | yes |
| XLS, XLSX, XLSB, XLSM, XLTX, XLTM, ODS, OTS | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| PPTX, PPTM | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | no | yes |
| ODP | yes | yes | no | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| PPT, PPS, PPSX, PPSM, POTX, POTM, OTP | yes | yes | no | yes | yes | yes | no | yes |
| JPG, JPEG, PNG, PSD, SVG, TIF, TIFF | yes | yes | no | yes | yes | yes | no | yes |
| BMP, GIF, WEBP, WMF, CDR, CMX, DJVU | yes | yes | no | yes | yes | yes | no | no |

- Archives (ZIP, TAR, 7Z, GZ, LZ): `Sign` and `Search` process every document inside; `SignResult` then lists one `DocumentResultSignature` per document.
- PNG and JPG images can also carry an image digital signature (`ImageDigitalSignOptions`).
- `FileType.GetSupportedFileTypes()` returns the formats the library can open at run time.

**Features**

- Signing: one or many signatures per call, on all pages, one page or a page set; alignment, margins, rotation, transparency, borders and solid, gradient or texture backgrounds; signatures in Word headers and footers; PDF text as annotation, sticker or form field; a signature line for Word and Excel digital signatures (`DigitalSignatureAppearance`).
- PDF digital signatures: visible or invisible; reason, contact and location; SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512; RFC 3161 time stamps; long-term validation (`UseLtv`); several signatures in sequence; signing an externally computed hash (`ICustomSignHash`, for example with an HSM).
- Verification: text, barcode, QR code, digital and image digital signatures, and certificate files. Digital signatures are checked cryptographically, then against the criteria you set.
- Search: every signature type, several types at once, with predicates (`Func<BaseSignature, bool>`), in documents and archives.
- Update signatures found by `Search`, and delete them by object, ID or type.
- `GetDocumentInfo()`: file type, size, page count, page sizes and the signatures and form fields already in the document.
- Previews: `GeneratePreview(PreviewOptions)` renders pages as PNG, JPG or BMP; `Signature.GenerateSignaturePreview(PreviewSignatureOptions)` renders a signature before you sign.
- Saving: output password, PDF permissions, and conversion to another format of the same family, to PDF or to images (`SaveOptions` and its subclasses).
- Loading: password-protected documents, explicit file type, streams, and control of external resources (`LoadOptions`).
- Events (`SignStarted`, `SignProgress`, `SignCompleted` and the matching verify and search events), process cancellation, and logging through `ILogger`.

**Code patterns**

Sign with visible text:

```csharp
using System.Drawing;
using GroupDocs.Signature;
using GroupDocs.Signature.Domain;
using GroupDocs.Signature.Options;

new License().SetLicense("GroupDocs.Signature.lic");

using (Signature signature = new Signature("contract.pdf"))
{
    TextSignOptions options = new TextSignOptions("John Smith")
    {
        Left = 100,
        Top = 100,
        Width = 200,
        Height = 40,
        ForeColor = Color.DarkBlue,
        Font = new SignatureFont { FamilyName = "Arial", Size = 14 }
    };
    SignResult result = signature.Sign("contract-signed.pdf", options);
    Console.WriteLine($"Created: {result.Succeeded.Count}, failed: {result.Failed.Count}");
}
```

Add a QR code and a barcode in one call:

```csharp
using (Signature signature = new Signature("invoice.docx"))
{
    List<SignOptions> options = new List<SignOptions>
    {
        new QrCodeSignOptions("https://example.com/invoices/123") { EncodeType = QrCodeTypes.QR, Left = 50, Top = 50 },
        new BarcodeSignOptions("123456789012") { EncodeType = BarcodeTypes.Code128, Left = 50, Top = 200 }
    };
    signature.Sign("invoice-signed.docx", options);
}
```

Sign a PDF with a certificate and a time stamp:

```csharp
using (Signature signature = new Signature("contract.pdf"))
{
    DigitalSignOptions options = new DigitalSignOptions("certificate.pfx")
    {
        Password = "certificate password",
        Reason = "Approved",
        Location = "Head office",
        // SHA-256 is the default; Sha384 and Sha512 are also available.
        HashAlgorithm = HashAlgorithm.Sha256,
        // Optional RFC 3161 time stamp. The time-stamp authority is contacted while signing.
        Signature = new PdfDigitalSignature { TimeStamp = new TimeStamp("https://freetsa.org/tsr", "", "") },
        // Visible signature rectangle on the first page.
        Left = 50,
        Top = 50,
        Width = 150,
        Height = 50
    };
    signature.Sign("contract-signed.pdf", options);
}
```

Verify a digital signature:

```csharp
using (Signature signature = new Signature("contract-signed.pdf"))
{
    // The PFX file, or a .cer file with the public certificate.
    DigitalVerifyOptions options = new DigitalVerifyOptions("certificate.pfx")
    {
        Password = "certificate password"
    };
    VerificationResult result = signature.Verify(options);
    Console.WriteLine(result.IsValid ? "Valid" : "Not valid");
}
```

Search for signatures:

```csharp
using (Signature signature = new Signature("contract-signed.pdf"))
{
    foreach (DigitalSignature digital in signature.Search<DigitalSignature>(SignatureType.Digital))
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{digital.Certificate?.Subject}, signed {digital.SignTime}, valid: {digital.IsValid}");
    }
    foreach (QrCodeSignature qrCode in signature.Search<QrCodeSignature>(SignatureType.QrCode))
    {
        Console.WriteLine($"{qrCode.EncodeType.TypeName} on page {qrCode.PageNumber}: {qrCode.Text}");
    }
}
```

Load options, streams, logging and errors:

```csharp
using GroupDocs.Signature.Logging;

LoadOptions loadOptions = new LoadOptions
{
    Password = "document password",
    // External resources are skipped by default. Allow only the addresses you trust.
    WhitelistedResources = new List<string> { "https://cdn.example.com/images/" }
};
SignatureSettings settings = new SignatureSettings(new ConsoleLogger())
{
    LogLevel = LogLevel.Error | LogLevel.Warning
};
try
{
    using (Stream input = File.OpenRead("protected.docx"))
    using (Stream output = File.Create("protected-signed.docx"))
    using (Signature signature = new Signature(input, loadOptions, settings))
    {
        signature.Sign(output, new TextSignOptions("John Smith") { Left = 100, Top = 100 });
    }
}
catch (GroupDocsSignatureException ex)
{
    // For example a wrong password, an expired certificate or an unreachable time-stamp authority.
    Console.WriteLine(ex.Message);
}
```
